body.statement:
For every simple graph \(G\) on \(n\geq1\) vertices and every \(S\subseteq V\), the exact-pencil handle is valid for the graph gadget. Writing \(T=V\setminus S\), \(a=16/25\), \(h_0(z)=z^2-p-r\), \(h_1(z)=z^3+az-ar\), \(c_i=a\) on \(S\), and \(c_i=1\) on \(T\), one has the polynomial identity
\[
 \det(zI_{3n}-B_{\pi_S})
 =z^{,n-|S|}\det\!\left(
   \operatorname{diag}(h_1(z)I_S,h_0(z)I_T)
   -zg\operatorname{diag}(c_i)A_G\right).
\]
On each critical disk centered at \(\zeta_\pm=(-3\pm\mathrm i\sqrt{91})/10\) with radius \(1/16\), the \(T\)-block Schur complement has no pole. The scalar coordinate \(f_\delta(z)=h_1(z)/(az)\) has, for every \(|y|\leq1/8\), a unique analytic inverse \(z=z_{\delta,\pm}(y)\) in the corresponding disk, with nonzero derivative. Under \(y=gw\), analytic zero multiplicities are preserved and the critical determinant is
\[
 \det\!\left(wI_S-A_G[S,S]-E(z_{\delta,\pm}(gw))\right),
 \qquad \|E(z)\|_2\leq4gn^2.
\]
For a suitable \(t\in[-3/4,-1/2]\), the rectangle \(-n-1<\operatorname{Re}w<t\), \(|\operatorname{Im}w|<1\) contains a zero of this determinant if and only if \(S\notin\mathcal I(G)\). Consequently, every independent intended assignment has all critical roots of modulus at most \(1-\delta/10\), whereas every non-independent intended assignment has a root of modulus at least \(1+g/20\). All its noncritical roots have modulus less than \(9/10\). Finally, an admissible assignment containing a root-only permutation cycle has spectral radius greater than \(1/(2g)\), and an admissible assignment with no root-only cycle but with a local \(u_i\)-\(w_i\) swap has an eigenvalue with real part greater than \(5/4\).
body.proof_tex:
Put \(r_0=15/16\), so \(r=r_0(1-\delta)\), and put
\[
 b=-p-r=\frac58+\frac{15}{16}\delta,
 \qquad d_0(z)=\frac{h_0(z)}z=z+\frac bz,
 \qquad f_\delta(z)=\frac{h_1(z)}{az}=\frac{z^2}{a}+1-\frac rz.
\]
We first derive the exact pencil from the normalized-candidate and graph-gadget definitions. If \(i\notin S\), the three eigenvector equations for \(B_{\pi_S}\) are
\[
 zu_i=v_i+w_i+g\sum_j(A_G)_{ij}u_j,
 \qquad zv_i=pu_i,
 \qquad zw_i=ru_i.
\]
Eliminating \(v_i,w_i\) gives
\[
 h_0(z)u_i=zg\sum_j(A_G)_{ij}u_j.
\]
If \(i\in S\), row normalization uses \(W_G[v_i,u_i]=-p\), and the equations are
\[
 zu_i=p^{-1}v_i,
 \qquad zv_i=u_i-w_i-g\sum_j(A_G)_{ij}u_j,
 \qquad zw_i=ru_i.
\]
Since \(-p^{-1}=a\), elimination gives
\[
 h_1(z)u_i=azg\sum_j(A_G)_{ij}u_j.
\]
Performing these eliminations at determinant level contributes one factor \(z\) for every unswitched vertex and no such factor for a switched vertex. Hence, for \(z\neq0\),
\[
 \det(zI_{3n}-B_{\pi_S})
 =z^{,n-|S|}\det\!\left(
   \operatorname{diag}(h_1(z)I_S,h_0(z)I_T)
   -zg\operatorname{diag}(c_i)A_G\right).
\]
Both sides are monic polynomials of degree \(3n\), so equality away from \(z=0\) extends to the asserted polynomial identity, including all zero multiplicities.

We next certify the Schur complement. On either disk \(|z-\zeta_\pm|\leq1/16\), one has \(|z|\geq15/16\). Since every adjacency submatrix has operator norm at most \(n\),
\[
 |d_0(z)|\geq |z|-\frac b{|z|}
 \geq\frac{13}{48}-\delta,
\]
and therefore
\[
 \sigma_{\min}\!\left(d_0(z)I_T-gA_G[T,T]\right)
 \geq\frac{13}{48}-\delta-gn>\frac14.
\]
Here the last inequality follows from
\[
 \varepsilon_n\leq2^{-44},\qquad
 gn=\frac{n}{2^{80}(n+1)^8}<2^{-80},
 \qquad \delta\leq2^{-132}.
\]
Thus the inverse exists throughout both closed disks and has norm at most \(4\). Dividing the \(S\)-rows by \(az\), the \(T\)-rows by \(z\), and taking the \(T\)-block Schur complement gives
\[
 \Phi_S(z)=f_\delta(z)I_S-gA_G[S,S]
 -g^2A_G[S,T]\bigl(d_0(z)I_T-gA_G[T,T]\bigr)^{-1}A_G[T,S].
\]
With
\[
 E(z)=gA_G[S,T]\bigl(d_0(z)I_T-gA_G[T,T]\bigr)^{-1}A_G[T,S],
\]
the submatrix norm bound and the inverse bound imply
\[
 \|E(z)\|_2\leq4gn^2=:\eta.
\]
This proves the asserted absence of poles uniformly in \(G\) and \(S\).

It remains to justify the inverse coordinate and multiplicity statement. Work first at \(\zeta=\zeta_+\); conjugation gives the other disk. Since \(f_0(\zeta)=0\), direct algebra yields
\[
 F:=f_0'(\zeta)=\frac{3\zeta^2+a}{a\zeta},
 \qquad |F|^2=\frac{3913}{256}>\left(\frac{39}{10}\right)^2.
\]
For \(v=z-\zeta\) with \(|v|\leq1/16\), one has \(|f_0''(z)|<6\); hence
\[
 f_\delta(\zeta+v)=Fv+R_0(v)+\frac{r_0\delta}{\zeta+v},
 \qquad |R_0(v)|\leq3|v|^2.
\]
On \(|v|=1/16\), the linear term is larger than \(39/160\), whereas, for \(|y|\leq1/8\),
\[
 |R_0(v)|+\left|\frac{r_0\delta}{\zeta+v}\right|+|y|
 \leq\frac3{256}+\delta+\frac18<\frac{39}{160}.
\]
The boundary-zero-count lemma applied to the homotopy from \(Fv\) to \(f_\delta(\zeta+v)-y\) shows that the latter has exactly one zero in the disk. Moreover,
\[
 |f_\delta'(\zeta+v)-F|\leq6|v|+2\delta<\frac12<|F|,
\]
so the derivative is nonzero. The unique solution \(z_\delta(y)\) is consequently analytic in \(y\).

The same estimates also give explicit radial control. From the preceding equation and \(|v|\leq1/16\),
\[
 \left(\frac{39}{10}-\frac3{16}\right)|v|\leq |y|+\delta,
 \qquad |v|\leq\frac{|y|+\delta}{3}.
\]
Define
\[
 \beta=F^{-1}=\frac{a\zeta}{3\zeta^2+a},
 \qquad \gamma=-\frac{3/5}{3\zeta^2+a}.
\]
Rearranging the scalar equation and using \(|\beta|<1/3\) gives
\[
 |z_\delta(y)-\zeta-\beta y-\gamma\delta|
 \leq(|y|+\delta)^2.
\]
The exact coefficients satisfy
\[
 \operatorname{Re}(\overline\zeta\beta)=-\frac8{43},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Im}(\overline\zeta\beta)=\frac{72\sqrt{91}}{3913},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Re}(\overline\zeta\gamma)=-\frac9{43}.
\]
Since
\[
 \bigl||\zeta+v|-1-\operatorname{Re}(\overline\zeta v)\bigr|
 \leq |v|^2,
\]
we obtain the disk-uniform expansion
\[
 |z_\delta(y)|=1-\frac9{43}\delta
 +\operatorname{Re}\!\left[
   \left(-\frac8{43}+\mathrm i\frac{72\sqrt{91}}{3913}\right)y\right]+R,
 \qquad |R|\leq4(|y|+\delta)^2. \tag{1}
\]

If \(z\) is a critical zero of \(\det\Phi_S\), a unit nullvector and the displayed inverse bound give
\[
 |f_\delta(z)|\leq gn+4g^2n^2<\frac18.
\]
Writing \(f_\delta(z)=gw\), uniqueness of the inverse coordinate gives \(z=z_\delta(gw)\), and
\[
 \Phi_S(z)=g\left(wI_S-A_G[S,S]-E(z_\delta(gw))\right). \tag{2}
\]
Because \(f_\delta'(z)\neq0\), the map \(w\mapsto z_\delta(gw)\) is locally biholomorphic. The eliminated \(T\)-block determinant and all row-scaling factors are nonzero on the critical disk. Equation (2), with its nonzero scalar factor \(g^{|S|}\), therefore proves equality of the zero order of the full characteristic polynomial in \(z\) and the zero order of the displayed determinant in \(w\). Thus multiplicities are preserved rather than merely counted setwise.

We now perform the negative-mode homotopy. If \(S\notin\mathcal I(G)\), choose an edge \(ij\) in \(G[S]\). The unit vector \((e_i-e_j)/\sqrt2\) has Rayleigh quotient \(-1\), so
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(A_G[S,S])\leq-1.
\]
Among the at most \(n\) real eigenvalues, choose
\(t\in[-3/4,-1/2]\) at distance at least \(1/[8(n+1)]\) from all of them: the eigenvalues divide this interval of length \(1/4\) into at most \(n+1\) gaps, and the midpoint of a largest gap has the stated separation. On the boundary of
\[
 \mathcal Q_t=\{w:-n-1<\operatorname{Re}w<t,\ |\operatorname{Im}w|<1\},
\]
normality of the real symmetric adjacency matrix gives
\[
 \left\|(wI_S-A_G[S,S])^{-1}\right\|_2\leq8(n+1).
\]
Indeed the right side of the rectangle has the chosen spectral separation, the horizontal sides have imaginary part of magnitude one, and the left side is at distance at least two because \(\|A_G[S,S]\|_2\leq n-1\). Hence
\[
 8(n+1)\eta=32gn^2(n+1)<1.
\]
The pencils
\[
 wI_S-A_G[S,S]-sE(z_\delta(gw)),\qquad 0\leq s\leq1,
\]
are therefore nonsingular on \(\partial\mathcal Q_t\). They are analytic there because \(|gw|<1/8\) on the closed rectangle and the already proved Schur denominator never vanishes. The boundary-zero-count lemma now preserves the number of zeros with multiplicity. At \(s=0\), the eigenvalue \(\lambda_{\min}(A_G[S,S])\) lies in \(\mathcal Q_t\), so at \(s=1\) at least one zero persists. Conversely, if \(S\in\mathcal I(G)\), then \(A_G[S,S]=0\), and a unit nullvector at any zero of (2) gives \(|w|\leq\eta<1/2\); thus no such zero lies in \(\mathcal Q_t\). This proves the claimed if and only if.

At any retained zero, the same unit-nullvector argument and normality give
\[
 \operatorname{dist}\!\left(w,\operatorname{spec}(A_G[S,S])\right)\leq\eta,
 \quad |\operatorname{Im}w|\leq\eta,
 \quad \operatorname{Re}w<t\leq-\frac12,
 \quad |w|\leq2(n+1).
\]
Since \(72\sqrt{91}/3913<1/5\), applying (1) with \(y=gw\) yields
\[
 |z|\geq1+\frac4{43}g-\frac9{43}\delta
 -g\eta-4\bigl(2g(n+1)+\delta\bigr)^2.
\]
Using \(\delta/g=\varepsilon_n\leq2^{-44}\) and
\(g(n+1)^2\leq2^{-86}\), the total subtracted quantity after the leading \(4g/43\) is less than \((4/43-1/20)g\). Thus \(|z|\geq1+g/20\). If \(S\in\mathcal I(G)\), then \(|w|\leq\eta\), so \(|y|\leq4g^2n^2\), and (1), together with
\[
 \frac{g^2n^2}{\delta}=\varepsilon_n n^2\leq2^{-44},
\]
gives \(|z|\leq1-\delta/10\). The conjugate disk has the same bounds.

For completeness, we locate every noncritical root. At \(g=\delta=0\), an unswitched vertex has characteristic polynomial
\[
 z\left(z^2+\frac58\right),
\]
and a switched vertex has characteristic polynomial
\[
 (z-3/5)(z-\zeta_+)(z-\zeta_-).
\]
On the three contours \(|z|=9/10\) and \(|z-\zeta_\pm|=1/16\), direct root-distance products bound each relevant local determinant below by \(3/1000\). Every \(2\)-by-\(2\) cofactor of the local resolvents has modulus at most \(8\), hence every local adjugate has operator norm at most \(24\), and the block-diagonal resolvent norm is less than \(8192\). Changing \(\delta\) and adding the graph coupling changes the block diagonal matrix by operator norm at most \(2\delta+gn\), while
\[
 8192(2\delta+gn)<1.
\]
The boundary-zero-count lemma therefore shows that exactly \(3n-2|S|\) roots lie in \(|z|<9/10\) and exactly \(|S|\) roots lie in each critical disk. These counts sum to \(3n\), so no root is omitted.

It remains to exclude unintended admissible assignments. A nontrivial permutation cycle follows a nonzero off-diagonal entry of \(W_G\). Since each leaf \(v_i\) or \(w_i\) has only its root \(u_i\) as an off-diagonal neighbor, a cycle containing a leaf must be the corresponding two-cycle. Every admissible permutation is therefore a disjoint union of fixed points, local \(u_i\)-\(v_i\) swaps, local \(u_i\)-\(w_i\) swaps, and cycles using roots only.

Suppose first that a nonempty set \(C\) of roots belongs to root-only cycles. After putting those roots first,
\[
 B_\pi=g^{-1}H+E_0,
 \qquad H=\begin{pmatrix}P&R\\0&0\end{pmatrix},
\]
where \(P\) is the permutation matrix of the root cycles and each row of \(R\) has the two entries \(-1\) at the leaves of the selected original root. Directly from the normalized rows, the remaining entries have modulus at most \(2\), and counting their supports gives \(\|E_0\|_2\leq\|E_0\|_{\mathrm F}\leq6n\). Since \(\|P^{-1}R\|_2=\sqrt2\), the shear
\[
 Q=\begin{pmatrix}I&-P^{-1}R\\0&I\end{pmatrix}
\]
satisfies
\[
 Q^{-1}HQ=\operatorname{diag}(P,0),
 \qquad \|Q\|_2\|Q^{-1}\|_2<6.
\]
Consequently
\[
 Q^{-1}(gB_\pi)Q=\operatorname{diag}(P,0)+F_0,
 \qquad \|F_0\|_2<36gn.
\]
On \(|z|=1/2\), the normal matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(P,0)\) has resolvent norm at most \(2\); because \(72gn<1\), the straight-line perturbation is boundary-invertible. The boundary-zero-count lemma preserves the \(|C|\) eigenvalues outside that circle. Hence \(\rho(B_\pi)>1/(2g)\).

Finally suppose there is no root-only cycle but some \(u_i\)-\(w_i\) swap. At zero graph coupling the possible local blocks are
\[
 M_0(\delta)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&1\\p&0&0\\r&0&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
 M_1(\delta)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1/p&0\\1&0&-1\\r&0&0\end{pmatrix},\quad
 M_2(\delta)=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&1/r\\p&0&0\\1&-1&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
At \(\delta=0\), their characteristic polynomials are, respectively,
\[
 z(z^2+5/8),\qquad
 (z-3/5)(z^2+(3/5)z+1),\qquad
 z^3-(16/15)z-5/3.
\]
The last polynomial has one real root in \((7/5,3/2)\), and its other two roots have real part less than \(-7/10\). On \(|z-3/2|=1/4\), its determinant modulus is greater than
\[
 \frac3{20}\left(\frac{39}{20}\right)^2>\frac12,
\]
whereas the first two polynomials have no zero in the disk. Every local adjugate on the contour has norm at most \(24\), so every local resolvent has norm at most \(64\). The combined change due to \(\delta\) and graph coupling has norm at most \(2\delta+gn\), and \(64(2\delta+gn)<1\). The boundary-zero-count lemma preserves one eigenvalue in this disk for every \(M_2\) block. Every point of the disk has real part greater than \(5/4\). Thus every such assignment is unstable. This completes the uniform no-pole, multiplicity, negative-mode, and unintended-assignment certification.
